---
name: ptk-vmr
description: "Configure or diagnose PTk virtual-monorepo discovery, repository aliases, workspace workflows, per-repository permissions and environment or credential conflicts. Use for Android repo membership or explicitly marked workspaces; preserve each member\u2019s ownership."
---

# PTk VMR workflows

First follow the [project discovery and execution guide](../../../docs/guides/agent-guide.rst). Apply it even when this skill is invoked directly; examples are syntax references, not project defaults.

1. Read [docs/guides/vmr.rst](../../../docs/guides/vmr.rst), [docs/reference/cli.rst](../../../docs/reference/cli.rst) and [docs/guides/configuration.rst](../../../docs/guides/configuration.rst). Run `ptk repos` and inspect each participating repository's root `.main.ptk.yml`. Confirm unique aliases and existing repository-relative `config_path` directories. From a repository, resolve its root `.git` symlink/junction or `gitdir:` file: only a target inside `.repo` establishes automatic membership. A parent `.repo` or ordinary Git worktree pointer is insufficient. At the workspace root, `.repo` directly activates VMR mode and `.repo/project.list` supplies members; if missing, report `repo sync` guidance, never scan recursively.
2. To initialize missing configs across a VMR, reuse the requested or established config-folder choice, asking only when missing. Preview `ptk init --config-dir PATH --dry-run`, then run `ptk init --config-dir PATH --yes`. The path is required and relative to each repository root; apply it to all new members. On a terminal, omission prompts once with no default. Omit DIRECTORY for all unconfigured checked-out members; supply DIRECTORY for just one project. Existing root entries are skipped, never rewritten, including invalid configs. Init uses the full member index, not `ptk repos` (which only lists configured members). Manual workspaces use explicit members or direct child Git repositories; do not scaffold build folders. Read the per-member results and count. Preserve the repository root as the execution directory.
3. Validate the workspace with `ptk validate` from its root; inspect a repository with `ptk ALIAS maintainer config show --sources`. Global options precede the alias. Inside a member directory of an automatically detected workspace, commands are routed to the deepest containing member: PTk prefixes its alias automatically, except for repository aliases, `ALIAS/...` arguments, `init`, `describe`, `jobs`, the workspace `self-service` commands (`completion`, `extension`, `doctor`, `creds`) and workspace workflows (`workflows/NAME.ptk.yml` at the workspace root). Other `self-service` commands such as `tools` act on the member.
4. Use workspace `self-service creds list` to find credential names; the vault belongs to the user and one `NAME.FIELD` value serves every repository. Listing does not unlock stores. Use `self-service creds set NAME FIELD` only when provisioning was requested. Credential tests run configured commands in each owning repository and can have external effects; inspect those commands first.
5. Tools: from the workspace root `ptk self-service tools [--job JOB] --dry-run` checks every repository (with `--job` only repositories defining that job); for one repository use `ptk ALIAS self-service tools --job JOB --dry-run` (or without `ALIAS` inside that member's directory), then the authorized installation. `ptk self-service hooks install|uninstall|status` at the root acts on every repository with a pre-commit configuration. Use `ptk jobs` to list every repository's jobs (role-filtered, `(gui)`/`(maintainer)` marked). Preview execution with `ptk ALIAS JOB --dry-run`.
6. Keep `environment.isolate: true` and `inherit_path: false`. Declare needed host variables with `keep`, configured variables with `set`, and credentials with step `secrets`. Prefer versioned managed tools. Do not fix missing tools by adding every cached installation to PATH. Use job-level `environment` only for deliberate overrides.
7. Inspect permitted commands with `ptk --help` (its first panel lists the VMR commands that act on every repository) and `ptk describe --json`; `ptk help` opens the advanced HTML help of the whole VMR. Use `variant list` and `validate --variants` where available. At the workspace root, `ptk report list [--history]` and `ptk report summary` read run status across members; `ptk maintainer configs-report` and `ptk maintainer version show` run in every repository after a per-repository maintainer check. Open a workflow report with `ptk report open --workflow NAME`. Export job reports through the owning repository (`ptk ALIAS report export`).
8. Verify the affected commands from the workspace root and a nested git-repo member. Check a nearby standalone repository, repeated initialization with existing configs preserved, and conflicting credential definitions. Re-run `ptk repos` after changing the member index. Use disposable workspaces for tests that create or modify files.
9. git-repo operations go through `ptk vmr` (see [cli reference](../../../docs/reference/cli.rst), section "git-repo commands"): `manifest [-o FILE] [--revision PROJECT=REV]` writes the revision-locked manifest of the current checkout; `init [URL] [-b REV] [--manifest FILE] --dir DIR` creates a new VMR outside any VMR; `reinit` switches the current one (refuses local changes without `--force`); `sync`, `status`, and `repo -- ARGS` for any other git-repo command. Prefer `ptk vmr init --manifest vmr_manifest.xml` to reproduce a CI build exactly.

For a manual VMR, create a workspace-root `.main.ptk.yml` containing `virtual_monorepo: true`, optionally `members: [nested/repo, other]`. It marks its containing directory, not its parent. Without `members`, inspect direct child directories only. Invoke grouped commands from that marked workspace; ordinary manual members remain standalone when invoked directly. A project's entry-level `virtual_monorepo: false` opts out of automatic membership and workspace listings. Omit it for automatic detection; do not add it to starter files by default. Discovery fields are literal entry metadata and cannot come from section files or `--set`.

For native GitHub templates, use [GitHub workflows](../ptk-github-workflows/SKILL.md). Preserve VMR checkout TODOs in setup and all execution jobs until the project supplies its checkout mechanism; the same member layout and revisions are required everywhere.

Use [versioning](../ptk-versioning/SKILL.md) for cross-repository version dependencies and [workflow authoring](../ptk-workflow-authoring/SKILL.md) for orchestration. Keep each call's configuration and identity in its owning repository. Synchronize agent resources in the intended member or workspace scope; installation into one does not change another. Each member’s external-config lock follows its own `repository.config_path`.

Maintainer lists are independent: each repository's configured folder contains
its own `maintainers.ptk.yml`; the VMR root may have a separate list for workspace
editor setup and restricted workspace workflows. Lists contain login strings.
Root membership does not grant member permissions. Workspace synchronization checks
all target permissions before writing; use a repository-qualified command for a
single permitted target. See [configuration](../../../docs/guides/configuration.rst).
